ai_insights.executive_summary: The test executed with 8 virtual users produced an overall error rate of 33.57% and only 74% SLA compliance, with 63 out of 242 transactions violating defined NFR targets. Latency spikes were observed, particularly for the Homepage launch (P90 1597 ms vs 250 ms SLA) and Add to Cart (P90 948 ms vs 600 ms SLA). Server‑side infrastructure telemetry was not available, limiting correlation of client‑side issues with host resources.

findings.title: Widespread Transaction Failures
findings.observation: 15 out of 20 listed transactions recorded 100% error rates (4‑4 samples each), contributing to an overall error rate of 33.57% and 63 SLA‑breaching transactions out of 242.
findings.likely_cause: Application‑level faults such as missing dependencies, misconfigured endpoints, or unhandled exceptions causing request failures.
findings.why_it_matters: Customers experience failed page loads or actions, directly impacting usability and conversion.
findings.recommendation: Enable detailed application logging, review error stacks for the failing endpoints, and fix the underlying code or configuration issues.
findings.validation: Re‑run the test after fixes and verify error rate drops below the 1% SLA target for each transaction.

findings.title: Excessive Response Times on Key Transactions
findings.observation: TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage P90 1597 ms exceeds 250 ms SLA by +538.8%; TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart P90 948 ms exceeds 600 ms SLA by +58.0%; TC02_T_09_Update_Cart_Quantities P90 885 ms exceeds 600 ms SLA by +47.5%.
findings.likely_cause: Processing delays or blocking calls within the application logic for those specific flows.
findings.why_it_matters: Slow page loads degrade user experience and can cause abandonment.
findings.recommendation: Profile the affected code paths to identify costly operations, optimize database queries or external service calls, and consider caching.
findings.validation: Re‑test and confirm P90 latencies fall within their respective SLA targets.

findings.title: Suboptimal Throughput and Request Instability
findings.observation: Peak throughput reached only 1.6 req/s at 20 seconds with 8 concurrent users, averaging 5.33 req/s overall; throughput fluctuated between 0.1 and 1.6 req/s across intervals, indicating request processing bottlenecks.
findings.likely_cause: Serializing bottlenecks, thread contention, or external service throttling limiting request processing rate.
findings.why_it_matters: Low throughput reduces capacity to serve users, leading to queued requests and increased latency under real‑world load.
findings.recommendation: Investigate thread pool configurations, external call timeouts, and consider asynchronous processing or scaling of backend services.
findings.validation: After adjustments, re‑run load test and verify throughput increases proportionally with concurrent users while latency remains stable.

findings.title: Missing Server‑Side Infrastructure Metrics
findings.observation: Server‑side infrastructure telemetry (CPU, memory, network, 5xx errors) was not configured, preventing correlation of client‑side latency and errors with host resource utilization.
findings.likely_cause: Incomplete monitoring setup for the test environment.
findings.why_it_matters: Without server metrics, it is impossible to determine whether performance issues stem from server saturation, application faults, or network problems.
findings.recommendation: Enable Azure Monitor (or equivalent) to collect host CPU, memory, request rates, and error codes, and re‑run the test to correlate client and server data.
findings.validation: Confirm that server metrics are available and show correlation with observed client‑side latency or error spikes.

capacity_planning.saturation_point: Observed concurrency of 8 threads; latency remained high (>900 ms) and error rates persisted, indicating saturation at this load level.
capacity_planning.analysis: With only 8 virtual users the test already showed high latency and errors; throughput did not scale and remained low, suggesting the system cannot handle even this modest load without degradation. Further testing with incremental concurrency would be needed to determine a safe operating point.

root_cause_assessment.evidence: 15 transactions with 100% error rate (4‑4 samples each), overall error rate 33.57%
root_cause_assessment.likely_cause: Application-level faults (missing dependencies, misconfiguration, unhandled exceptions)
root_cause_assessment.recommended_investigation: Enable application logs, examine stack traces for failing endpoints, verify dependencies and configurations.

root_cause_assessment.evidence: P90 breaches: Launch Homepage +538.8% (1597 ms vs 250 ms), Add Bulldog +58.0% (948 ms vs 600 ms), Update Cart Quantities +47.5% (885 ms vs 600 ms)
root_cause_assessment.likely_cause: Blocking or inefficient processing in those transaction paths
root_cause_assessment.recommended_investigation: Profile the affected code paths, identify costly operations (e.g., DB queries, external calls), and optimize.

recommendations.title: Resolve Widespread Transaction Failures
recommendations.why: 15 endpoints exhibited 100% failure rates, driving overall error rate to 33.57% and breaching SLA for 63 transactions.
action: Enable detailed application logging for all endpoints
Review and correct missing dependencies or configuration issues
Implement retry or fallback handling where appropriate
recommendations.expected_impact: Error rate reduced below 1% SLA target, restoring transaction success and improving user experience.
recommendations.validation: Re‑run load test and verify error rate per transaction <1% and overall SLA compliance >90%

recommendations.title: Reduce Response Times for Homepage, Add‑to‑Cart, and Cart Update
recommendations.why: P90 latencies exceed SLA by up to +538.8%, directly impacting user‑perceived performance.
action: Profile the Homepage launch, Add‑to‑Cart, and Cart Update flows
Identify and optimize slow database queries or external service calls
recommendations.expected_impact: P90 latencies brought within SLA limits (≤250 ms for Homepage, ≤600 ms for Add‑to‑Cart and Cart Update).
recommendations.validation: Re‑execute test and confirm P90 values meet SLA targets.

recommendations.title: Activate Infrastructure Telemetry for Correlated Analysis
recommendations.why: Lack of server‑side metrics prevents determining whether latency or errors stem from host saturation or application faults.
action: Configure Azure Monitor to collect host CPU, memory, request rates, and HTTP 5xx errors
Ensure metrics are exported to the test reporting system
Re‑run load test with monitoring enabled
recommendations.expected_impact: Ability to correlate client‑side symptoms with server resource utilization, guiding precise remediation.
recommendations.validation: Verify that server metrics are present in the test report and show correlation with observed latency or error spikes.

executive_summary.assessment_text:
• Overall SLA compliance was 74% (179 of 242 transactions met targets) with an error rate of 33.57%.
• Fifteen endpoints showed 100% failure rates, driving the majority of SLA breaches.
• Key transactions exceeded latency SLAs by up to +538.8% (Homepage launch P90 1 597 ms vs 250 ms SLA).
• Server‑side monitoring was absent, limiting root‑cause analysis of latency and failures.
assessment_bullets: Overall SLA compliance was 74% (179 of 242 transactions met targets) with an error rate of 33.57%.
Fifteen endpoints showed 100% failure rates, driving the majority of SLA breaches.
Key transactions exceeded latency SLAs by up to +538.8% (Homepage launch P90 1 597 ms vs 250 ms SLA).
Server‑side monitoring was absent, limiting root‑cause analysis of latency and failures.
conclusions: The system failed to meet reliability and performance objectives under a modest load of 8 virtual users.
Application‑level faults are the primary driver of transaction failures and high latency.
Without server‑side metrics, infrastructure contributions cannot be ruled out.

observations: Total of 56 samples were executed across the listed transactions, with 0 passing and 56 failing (100% error rate for each).
Throughput remained low and unstable, peaking at 1.6 req/s with 8 concurrent users and averaging 5.33 req/s overall.
recommendations: Investigate and resolve application‑level faults causing universal transaction failures before attempting load‑scale optimizations.

observations: Overall P90 latency was 955 ms, exceeding the default 500 ms SLA by +91%; specific transactions such as Launch Homepage (P90 1597 ms) and Add‑to‑Cart (P90 948 ms) breached their individual SLAs by +538.8% and +58.0% respectively.
Average response times varied widely from 207 ms to 2 214 ms across transactions, indicating inconsistent performance.
recommendations: Focus optimization efforts on the high‑latency transactions identified (Launch Homepage, Add‑to‑Cart, Update Cart Quantities) to bring their P90 values within SLA limits.
